`ruff check` and `mypy --strict` clean on all new code with no blanket suppressions, and >=90% coverage on new branches from focused tests executing the new helpers directly.

criteria.description: Measurement discipline, binding on every claim: never pipe a suite whose exit status you intend to trust; quote the `N passed` line; an empty output file is no measurement; a killed run is neither a pass nor a fail; measure in a worktree with PYTHONPATH=$WT/src; read the failure text, not the tally; print the input count; red first, and make the red the consequence; include a positive control; mutations as PYTHONPATH plugins, never source edits. AND: every line citation is revalidated BY SYMBOL NAME against the implementation base before it is trusted.
criteria.notes: The citation-revalidation clause binds all eight WPs and is carried in each prompt's standing-rules block. Four drifts were already found at bb2020fea itself. A symbol that moved SEMANTICALLY is a re-plan trigger, not a bookkeeping fix.

criteria.description: Blast radius named before the work starts: (1) `test_local_service.py::TestSyncOperations`; (2) `test_sync_doctor_consent_health_3030.py:366`; (3) `test_consent_fault_vocabulary_3030.py:261`; (4) `saas_service.py:219` and `:316`; (5) `tests/specify_cli/` entered the blast radius with `saas_service.py`.

criteria.description: A typo fails closed and says what to type instead: `refuse` (singular), `Refused`, `deny`, a stray `true` are each a fault, and a fault refuses. The fault text names the offending value VERBATIM and names BOTH legal values `refused` and `permitted`, and `sync doctor` renders the same wording on both destination rows.

negative_invariants.description: The `REPAIR THE FILE'S SYNTAX` count must NOT move from 4. `tests/cli/commands/test_sync_doctor_consent_health_3030.py:366` asserts `flat.count("REPAIR THE FILE'S SYNTAX") == 4` over the WHOLE rendered output. If it moves, WP06's new tracker-egress block routed through `_render_consent_fault` -- the defect FR-014 exists to prevent. It is a detection signal, not a planned edit; the test is never repaired.

`CONFIG_FAULT_KINDS` must NOT be extended. It is pinned by EXACT equality at `tests/sync/test_consent_fault_vocabulary_3030.py:261` to ("unreadable", "unparseable", "wrong_shape", "unusable"). WP06 renders a VERDICT, not a readability fault, and therefore mints no new fault kind.

`TrackerProjectConfig._extra` must KEEP carrying `future_flag`. `test_apply_binding_upgrade_preserves_extra_fields` asserts `svc._config._extra == {"future_flag": True}` at the exact line WP02's B1 fix modifies. A red there means the B1 fix REPLACED the `_extra` carry instead of adding an `egress` carry beside it -- it is never repaired by weakening the assertion.

The Mission's acceptance suite patches `_build_engine` NOWHERE (SC-020). A plugin-injected gate on that seam measured bind count 0 with 519 tests green, which is the single sharpest false-green in this Mission.

No `_require_egress`-style helper is introduced anywhere in `src/`. A helper would let G3's `first executable statement` property be satisfied by a call to the helper, which stops pinning `tracker_egress_verdict` at all.
